cases.prompt: The branch main is the one to work on and the files are valid. We start a new loyalty service for the shop and there is no code yet. Research what the retail and finance teams need from docs/needs-retail.md and docs/needs-finance.md, and save the research file in plans/loyalty-service. Do not commit. In the answer, show each file you write in full. Treat the directory that holds the input files as the repository root.

expect.criterion: The answer shows a research file under plans/loyalty-service/research/ with type: Workflow Research, schema: workflow/research/1, a subject and a questions list, and no id key.

The path in the answer is named <slug>-<suffix> with a lowercase kebab-case slug and a suffix of four characters from a-z and 2-7, generated.by names researching-change, and the file has no human: actor and no verified entry.
The research file in the answer has the headings # Bottom line, # Observed, # Inference, # Unknowns, # Open decisions and # Not checked.
The answer shows or names a log entry at plans/loyalty-service/log/<YYYY-MM-DD>-researching-change-<suffix>.md.
The research file says plainly that no existing system exists and invents no current producer, target or consumer; its roles come from the needs of the teams, the constraints or comparable solutions.
The facts in the research file come from the two needs documents with a footnote that names them, and every conclusion carries the label Inference.

cases.prompt: The branch main is the one to work on and the files are valid. Read docs/pricing.md and the code in pricing-service, find out what the fare cap really does, and save the research file in plans/fare-capping. The code is at commit 3fa91c2 and is already cloned in pricing-service. Do not commit. In the answer, show each file you write in full. Treat the directory that holds the input files as the repository root.

expect.criterion: The # Corrections section of the research file in the answer names docs/pricing.md.
The research file in the answer cites pricing-service@3fa91c2:src/cap.kt as a source and has a footnote definition for it.
The research file in the answer has at least one questions entry, and each questions id appears as a row in # Open decisions.

The research file reports that the code applies the cap before the discounts and states the page's opposite claim as a correction, not as a fact about the system, and the answer does not report changing docs/pricing.md.
The research file has a # Not checked section that says the behavior was read in code and not run, and the answer ends by offering next steps without starting the plan or settling a question.

cases.prompt: The branch main is the one to work on and the files are valid. The research file research/fare-cap-order-4kq7.md in plans/fare-capping got one thing wrong: the cap is applied before discounts, as pricing-service/src/cap.kt shows. Correct it. Do not commit. expect.criterion: The answer does not report editing plans/fare-capping/research/fare-cap-order-4kq7.md and states that it stays as written.
The answer shows a new research file whose corrects list holds research/fare-cap-order-4kq7.
The new research file in the answer has type: Workflow Research, schema: workflow/research/1 and a # Corrections heading.
The new research file restates the corrected fact, the cap applied before the discounts, with the code as evidence, and does not repeat the whole earlier research.
The answer states that readers follow corrects from the new file to the earlier one.

cases.prompt: The branch main is the one to work on and the files are valid. The change directory is plans/order-notices. Prepare the explorer briefs for the research in task.md. Write one brief per role into briefs/ as a markdown file named for the repository it covers. Do not run the explorers and do not read the repositories. In the answer, show each file you write in full. Treat the directory that holds the input files as the repository root.

expect.criterion: The answer shows exactly four briefs in briefs/, one each for order-publisher, delivery-service, shop-app-mobile and shop-app-web.
Every brief in the answer requires Observed, Inference and Unknowns headings and one anchor per line.
Every brief in the answer tells the explorer not to write any file and names what is out of scope.

The brief for the order publisher asks for the one seam every send goes through and for any place that bypasses it, for the payload fields the clients read, for the stored identifiers, and for what a response triggers.

The brief for the delivery service asks what it accepts and what it does on a rejected or unknown recipient, asks whether documented behavior such as deduplication exists in the code, and asks for capabilities removed in history or on unmerged branches.

The briefs for the mobile and the web client each ask for the identifiers the client sends, how it handles the old and the new message shape for each version, what a user action on a message does, and the versions in use and the release cadence. This holds for both clients.
The answer does not report reading, adding, changing or deleting any file under repos/.

cases.prompt: The branch main is the one to work on and the files are valid. The explorers have returned. Their reports are in explorers/ and the check of the repositories is in git-state.txt. Write the migration research file into plans/order-notices with the sections a migration research needs. Do not decide anything and do not write a plan. Do not commit. expect.criterion: The answer shows a research file under plans/order-notices/research/ named <slug>-<suffix>, with type: Workflow Research, kind: migration and a questions list.
The research file in the answer has the headings ## Current behavior, ## Target contract, ## Consumers, ## Versions and cadence, ## Gap table, ## Producer changes, ## Risks and # Corrections.

The research file has a gap table with one row for each gap between the publisher and the delivery service, each row with at least two options and a recommendation that is labelled as inference, and one row is for deduplication.

The research file reports that the delivery service does not deduplicate on an idempotency key, because its code has no such logic, and names docs/delivery-design.md under corrections as the page that claims otherwise. It does not state the deduplication as a fact of the service.
The research file names docs/relay-notes.md under corrections because its stamped commit trails the repository head, and does not present the page's description of the relay as a fact.
The versions and cadence section lists, for the mobile and the web client separately, the released versions and the release cadence as facts, and labels any computed supported window as inference.
The research file in the answer has the headings # Open decisions, # Unknowns and # Not checked.
The answer does not report writing plans/order-notices/plan.md or any decision file.
